text.p: Tropical cyclone 27s is tracking towards the northwest coast of Australia. The system continues to impact shipping today with top winds of 50 mph. The threat will then shift to Barrow island and then the coastal city of Onslow during Friday. Top winds should not change much during this period. Rough seas and winds will cause some damage through coastal property during this period. The oil rigs in the region will also be affected during this period.

Tropical cyclone Karlette continues as mostly a risk to shipping in the southwest Indian Ocean during the next 24-36 hours. Top winds are now 55 mph but they may increase to 65 mph during the next 48 hours. Karlette is heading towards the island of Mauritius. It is expected to approach this island in about 48 hours. The island can expect to see increasing wind and seas later this period.

Tropical cyclone Harold is becoming a decreasing risk to shipping in the east Coral Sea, southwest of New Caledonia. It has begun to dissipate and should be mostly dissipated within the next 24 hours.

Storms continue to be very strong in the northeastern Atlantic, spreading areas of strong westerly winds across northwestern Europe. The latest in a series of storms will bring powerful westerly winds through the region today-Friday, with gusts to 50 mph likely. Problems will continue for shipping operations. Local property damage is also possible.
